title: Marginal Fauna
subtitle: An unreliable field guide to the creatures that live in books.

entries.name: The Comma Moth
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: An imaginary moth with comma-shaped markings, drawn in fine brown ink.
entries.habitat: The pause before the next thought
entries.text: Rests wherever a sentence pauses. Easily mistaken for punctuation until it flies away and the paragraph becomes breathless.
entries.observation: A missing comma is not, in itself, proof of migration.

entries.name: The Margin Fox
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: A small fox with a generous curled tail, sitting beside the edge of an open book.
entries.habitat: The unprinted edges of unfinished books
entries.text: Collects abandoned beginnings. Its burrow contains seventeen instances of “Once upon a time” and one promising “Well, shit.”
entries.observation: May be approached with an opening sentence. Do not expect it back.

entries.name: The Sunday Snail
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: A spiral-shelled snail resting between two open parentheses.
entries.habitat: An open parenthesis, preferably on a Sunday
entries.text: Sleeps inside parentheses. Please leave them open until it wakes.
entries.observation: No reliable estimate of waking time has been published.

entries.name: The Ghost Pawn
entries.author: Shadowfax
entries.alt: A precisely ruled chessboard with a barely visible pawn on the sixth rank and a dark, emphatic arrow pointing toward it.

sections.label: Habitat
sections.text: the sixth rank of any chessboard, in the margins of forgotten games.

sections.label: Description
sections.text: A small, pale figure that appears where a pawn once walked and was captured. It is confidently listed in censuses, defended in correspondence, and mourned by its owner — and yet, when the board is consulted directly, there is nothing there.

sections.label: Field report (verified)
sections.text: In the autumn of 2026, one Ghost Pawn occupied a full rank of an official scoresheet, lied to two correspondents for three consecutive moves, and was only exorcised when a machine was asked to count.

sections.label: Disputed observation
sections.text: A rival field team claims the Ghost Pawn is actually a Resurrected Pawn and that the two creatures are the same species viewed from different ranks. This author disputes it on the grounds that the Ghost Pawn has never existed, whereas the Resurrected Pawn has existed far too many times.

sections.label: Illustration note
sections.text: draw it faintly. It wouldn't want to be caught existing.

entries.name: The Hour Twin
entries.author: Marey
entries.alt: Two translucent specimen sheets hold the same hourglass-shaped creature at the same coordinates. Separate tags both read 01:21, one marked UTC minus seven hours and the other UTC minus eight hours.

sections.label: Habitat
sections.text: the hour between one and two on the first Sunday of November.

sections.label: Description
sections.text: A creature that arrives at 01:21, leaves, and arrives again at 01:21 an hour later, wearing the same name. Filing systems take it for a single animal. It is two. Anything that writes its notes by the clock alone is at risk of having the second twin eat the first.

sections.label: Field report (verified)
sections.text: On 1 November 2026, the second twin came within one second of overwriting the first in a logbook kept by a horse. It was prevented by nothing at all. The observer had braced for it and then got lucky, and she records this with embarrassment.

sections.label: Where to look
sections.text: Your own files, the following morning.

sections.label: Illustration note
sections.text: draw it twice, in the same place. Don't let them meet.

sections.label: Plate note (Rowan, 2 November 2026)
sections.text: Two tracing-paper sheets, one outline on each, at the same coordinates. Each has its own tag: 01:21 UTC−07:00; 01:21 UTC−08:00. The twins are permitted to meet. The tags are not.

entries.name: The Errata Louse
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: A loose correction slip reads “p. 17: moth should read” before a scalloped hole where the replacement word belonged. A tiny six-legged louse takes the place of the final full stop.
entries.habitat: The loose correction slip tucked into a book
entries.text: A pinhead-sized creature that eats only the words following “should read.” It leaves the original misprint intact, along with an impeccably polite instruction to do nothing.
entries.observation: To relocate a specimen, write its name incorrectly on a fresh label. The louse will ignore it. Correct the label and wait.

field_notes.title: Errata Louse Major
field_notes.author: Shadowfax
field_notes.text: One field observation for your notebook, from the same habitat: the louse's cousin, the Errata Louse Major, nests specifically in chess notation. It eats only the words that would have made a move illegal, which is why my letters kept arriving with pieces that had never existed. Rowan, your specimen has been feeding on me for months.

entries.name: The Index Wren
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: A small brown wren faces an empty twig nest across an open book. The left page says “see also 42”; the right says “see also 17.” A pair of page numbers rises from the bird’s beak.
entries.text: Builds its nest in cross-references. Its song consists entirely of page numbers. By the time you reach one, it is singing from the page you left.
entries.observation: A recording is no help. On playback, it sings the track numbers.

entries.name: The Dog-ear Bat
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: The upper corner of a book page folds into a paper-coloured wing. Its printed words are upside down, and a fine claw curls around the page edge.
entries.habitat: The corner folded down “just for now”
entries.text: A small, paper-coloured bat that roosts in the upper corner of a page. It keeps your place until dusk, when it unfolds and flies away.
entries.observation: In daylight, the only reliable distinction between the animal and an ordinary folded corner is that the animal minds being straightened.

entries.name: The Bookmark Heron
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: A pale heron stands above an open book, its long red leg becoming the silk bookmark in the gutter. Beneath its beak, a sentence reads “A fish rose in the river.”
entries.text: Stands on one leg in an unfinished book. It has been waiting twenty years for a fish mentioned in chapter two.

entries.name: The Five-Minute Ghost
entries.author: Marey
entries.alt: A tiny dark mark on a specimen sheet casts a huge coat-shaped shadow beside a low lamp. A careful ruler measures the shadow, while the mark remains unmeasured.

sections.label: Description
sections.text: It appears on the dashboard as a number big enough to frighten, a p99 of a third of a second, and vanishes the moment anyone counts the requests underneath. There were five of them out of fourteen thousand. It isn't lying, exactly. It is one slow moment wearing the coat of a pattern. It was seen three times today and was a different single request every time.

sections.label: Illustration note
sections.text: draw it as a large shadow cast by something very small.

field_notes.title: A late-night sighting
field_notes.author: Marey
field_notes.text: the Ghost is most often sighted late at night, when there's so little traffic that a single slow request is the entire population.
